headline: SOCIAL'S SHARE OF HOLIDAY REVENUE IS GROWING 17 PERCENT AND PAID SEARCH'S IS GROWING 4.  INSIDE THE AFFILIATE LINE, CASHBACK SITES SEND MORE TRAFFIC THAN CREATORS, 36 PERCENT TO 22
deck: Adobe published its holiday forecast this morning.  275.1 billion dollars spent online in the United States across November and December, up 6.7 percent.  The total is not the useful part.  The useful part is which channels are growing their share of it, and which half of the creator channel is doing the work.
tldr: Adobe forecasts 275.1 billion dollars of American online holiday spending, with social's share of revenue growing 17 percent against paid search's 4, and within the affiliate channel cashback partners taking 36 percent of traffic to creators' 22.  Add a trackable code or cashback offer to every creator deal you sign this quarter, because that is the difference between the two halves of that channel.

Sprout Social asked 2,286 shoppers what makes them more likely to buy at Christmas: a promo code from a brand or influencer came first at 30 percent and a targeted social ad came last of six at 18.  Rewrite your creator briefs around a code plus the product genuinely being used on camera, and stop paying a premium for polish.

Agencies say Meta has been telling them its ranking treats two ads with the same look or the same opening hook as the same ad, though Meta declines to confirm how its models read individual assets.  Rebuild one live variant set this week so each version opens on a different subject and a different first frame, and add a still image to the set.

Zappi showed the Converse image to 250 people and almost a third connected it to lynching or the Klan unprompted, while two-thirds saw nothing wrong — and 46 percent of Black respondents saw the association.  Add a subgroup breakdown to every creative test you run before a campaign goes live, because the average is what signed this one off.

Deloitte's survey of 3,518 Americans puts purchase likelihood 2.5 times higher where the audience trusts the creator's recommendation and 1.2 times higher where they simply see the same creator repeatedly.  Score your creator shortlist on evidence of audience trust first, and treat a long contract as a way to lower cost rather than raise performance.

The Fortnite global final set a series record above a million people watching at once while hours watched fell 23.6 percent, because the channels carrying it went from 770 to 253.  Ask every live sponsorship seller for the peak and average number of people watching at once, the broadcast length and the number of channels counted, before you price the deal.

Taylor Swift premiered Patient Zero on CBS, pointed fans at three paid subscription services and put it on YouTube two days later, in the same week Spotify became the VMAs' first on-platform video partner.  Ask what your client's scoreboard actually counts before you set an upload time, and treat the free-platform date as a decision rather than a default.
